I give up.

I did not change `/work/putnam_2008_b5.lean`, and I did not compile it, because I don't have a proof I can formalize.

The statement is Putnam 2008 B5, which needs a real analytic argument. The natural route is to show that the derivative of `f` has absolute value 1 everywhere, using denominator bounds on nearby rationals, then conclude `f' = ±1` with a constant sign. From there, `f(0)` is an integer, and `f(q) - q` (or `f(q) + q`) is an integer on all rationals, so continuity forces a constant integer shift. I could not make the derivative step rigorous: the naive denominator-gap estimates give only a bound on `|f'|`, not its exact value. Formalizing the full argument in Lean with Mathlib, without the ability to look up library sources, is beyond what I can finish here.
